title: MIWA Compatible RFID Hotel Key Cards — Dual-Frequency Estate Matrix
summary: ProudTek RFID cards are fully compatible with MIWA hotel locks across the ALV2 series (13.56 MHz ISO/IEC 14443A), PR series (125 kHz legacy), and LD dual-credential locks using MIFARE Classic 1K, MIFARE Ultralight C, and EM4100 compatible chips. MIWA's market dominance in Japanese and Asian hotel properties often requires estates to manage both 13.56 MHz guest-room access and 125 kHz service-area credentials in parallel. Selecting incompatible chips for a dual-frequency MIWA estate creates operational fragmentation — guest rooms encode successfully but service staff cannot access common areas, or vice versa. This compatibility risk affects not just access control but guest satisfaction and operational efficiency. The compatibility matrix on this page maps every MIWA lock series to its radio frequency, supported chip families, encoding method and the exact ProudTek card SKU verified through internal MIWA-certified test encoding. Properties can consolidate dual-frequency inventory by specifying mixed-chip card orders that include both 13.56 MHz and 125 kHz credentials in a single shipment. Request a free MIWA test-card kit to validate compatibility on your specific lock hardware and estate frequency layout before production ordering.

sections.title: MIWA Lock Series and Frequency-Chip Compatibility Matrix
sections.intro: MIWA hotel estates typically operate across multiple frequencies — 13.56 MHz for guest-room security and 125 kHz for service-area access. Understanding your property's lock composition is essential before ordering credentials.

callout.label: Dual-frequency rule
callout.text: If your MIWA estate includes both ALV2 locks (13.56 MHz) and PR locks (125 kHz), you must order two separate card inventories or negotiate a mixed-batch arrangement with frequency-specific encoding per serial block.

sections.title: MIWA Dual-Frequency Estate Encoding Workflow
sections.intro: Properties spanning both 13.56 MHz ALV2 rooms and 125 kHz PR service areas must follow a two-stage encoding process to maintain access segregation.

items.label: Stage 1 — Estate frequency audit
items.text: Identify all MIWA lock models and their frequencies. Determine which doors are ALV2 (13.56 MHz), which are PR (125 kHz) and whether any LD dual-credential locks are installed.

items.label: Stage 2 — Chip and frequency selection
items.text: ProudTek recommends MIFARE Classic 1K for ALV2 and EM4100-compatible 125 kHz cards for PR. Dual-frequency staff receive synchronized batches with both chips encoded to a single physical card via LD encoder if available.

items.label: Stage 3 — Test-kit frequency validation
items.text: Receive 5-card sample kit with both 13.56 MHz and 125 kHz variants. Test guest-room ALV2 locks with 13.56 MHz cards and service-area PR locks with 125 kHz cards separately.

items.label: Stage 4 — Encoding station verification
items.text: Confirm your MIWA encoder or management software supports the selected frequencies. Legacy systems may require firmware updates to enable LD dual-frequency mode.

items.label: Stage 5 — Batch production with frequency separation
items.text: ProudTek manufactures and encodes cards in frequency-segregated batches, then packages by staff role (guest-room staff receive 13.56 MHz only; service staff receive 125 kHz only; or unified roles get LD dual-chip).

faq.question: What frequency does MIWA ALV2 operate on?
faq.answer: MIWA ALV2 series operates on 13.56 MHz using ISO/IEC 14443A, the same frequency standard as Saflok and most modern hotel RFID locks. The primary chip is MIFARE Classic 1K. Some ALV2 advanced models support MIFARE Ultralight C for enhanced compatibility.

faq.question: Can I use a single card to unlock both ALV2 and PR locks in a dual-frequency estate?
faq.answer: Not with standard single-frequency cards. ALV2 reads 13.56 MHz MIFARE chips and PR reads 125 kHz EM4100 chips — they operate on different frequencies and cannot be decoded by the same antenna. MIWA LD dual-credential locks can unlock with either frequency, but you still need separate physical cards or an expensive LD dual-chip card with both frequencies encoded. For most estates, frequency-segregated inventory is simpler and more cost-effective.

faq.question: What is an EM4100-compatible 125 kHz card, and which MIWA locks use it?
faq.answer: EM4100 is a legacy 125 kHz RFID standard used in MIWA PR series and older service-area access systems. EM4100-compatible cards are simple read-only credentials — the ID cannot be easily re-encoded without specialized equipment. ProudTek manufactures EM4100 cards for MIWA PR series compatibility. These cards typically cost 10-15% less than 13.56 MHz MIFARE cards but offer minimal security features.

faq.question: How do I know if my MIWA estate requires dual-frequency cards?
faq.answer: Check your lock inventory list. If you have both ALV2 series locks (typically labeled as such) and PR series locks, you have a dual-frequency estate. Create a floor plan marking which doors are ALV2 (13.56 MHz) and which are PR (125 kHz). Properties with only ALV2 or only PR need single-frequency cards exclusively.

faq.question: Can ProudTek encode MIWA-compatible cards on-site, or must encoding happen at the property?
faq.answer: ProudTek ships cards with the correct chip configuration but does not pre-encode guest-access credentials, as room keys require real-time PMS data including room number and occupancy status. Guest rooms must be encoded at the property using your MIWA encoder. However, ProudTek can pre-encode service-area access keys if the property provides access-group definitions.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for MIWA-compatible cards?
faq.answer: MIFARE Classic 1K cards for ALV2 start at 250 pieces; EM4100 125 kHz cards for PR series start at 300 pieces. Test-card kits of 5 pieces are available at no charge for new compatibility projects. Mixed-frequency orders typically require at least 500 total pieces (split between frequencies) due to encoder setup costs.

faq.question: How long does MIWA compatibility verification take?
faq.answer: The typical timeline from initial inquiry to bulk order approval is 12-16 business days. Estate frequency audit takes 2-3 days, test-kit shipment to Asia takes 4 days, frequency-segregated on-site validation takes 3-4 days, and artwork approval adds 4-5 days. Properties ordering plain white stock without custom printing can move from test-kit approval to bulk delivery in 10-12 business days.

faq.question: Does MIWA support MIFARE Plus or DESFire chips?
faq.answer: No. Standard MIWA ALV2 and PR firmware does not support MIFARE Plus, MIFARE DESFire or NFC chips. Only MIFARE Classic 1K (ALV2 at 13.56 MHz) and EM4100-compatible (PR at 125 kHz) are supported. Some newer MIWA systems may add MIFARE Ultralight C support in future firmware updates, but this is not currently documented in standard installations.

faq.question: What happens if I mix 13.56 MHz and 125 kHz cards in a dual-frequency estate?
faq.answer: Guest-room ALV2 locks will reject 125 kHz cards, and service-area PR locks will reject 13.56 MHz cards. This creates operational confusion where staff attempting to enter their designated access areas cannot open doors. The solution is frequency-aware issuing — provide guest-room staff only 13.56 MHz credentials and service staff only 125 kHz credentials, or use LD dual-credential capable cards if your encoders support it.
